Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The study focuses on developing assistive software (mouse/keyboard substitution, word prediction, accessibility adaptations) to enable PC use for people with motor impairments. It is framed around utility and accessibility, not entertainment or fun, and is created by HCI researchers using contextual inquiry with disabled users, not by clinicians or as a repurposed entertainment game. This aligns best with a mostly utility-first design where the primary utilitarian mechanics are designed first.

        (1) unstructured play (i.e., no rules, making art),
        (2) semi-structured play (i.e., playground activities),
        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: The study tasks are tightly specified performance tests: a classic Fitts-law style pointing task with predefined target sizes, distances, and randomized sequences, and a structured text-entry task where participants must copy given phrases and press ENTER to proceed. These are rigid, experimenter-controlled tasks with fixed rules and no improvisation or house-rule flexibility, best matching a game with rigid rules.

reasoning: The study tasks (mouse pointing test and typing test) are continuous individual activities without alternating turns or structured action phases between agents; participants simply perform actions as quickly and accurately as possible, which best matches an entirely simultaneous/race-like structure.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely synchronous (i.e., real time strategy game),
        (2) mostly synchronous with a few asynchronous affordances (i.e., league of legends),
        (3) equal mix of synchronous and asynchronous affordances (i.e., helldivers 2),
        (4) mostly asynchronous with few synchronous affordances (i.e. cookie clicker),
        (5) entirely asynchronous (i.e., chess by postage mail)
reasoning: The study is about using a Palm-based Remote Commander and text-entry tools to control a PC and perform typing and pointing tests. All interactions are single-user, device-to-PC input tasks (mouse pointing, typing phrases, word prediction), with no multiplayer, turn-taking, or real-time co-play elements. These are entirely asynchronous human–computer interactions rather than synchronous multi-user or game-like environments, so the design best matches an entirely asynchronous setup.

reasoning: The study is about assistive handheld software (Remote Commander, keyboards, word prediction) to help people with neuromuscular disorders use their PCs. There is no game or competition; tasks are individual performance tests and case studies focused on enabling users. This maps best to an entirely collaborative design, as all interaction is user + system working toward a single goal with no competitive elements.

        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),
        (4) mostly asymmetrical (i.e., tag),
        (5) entirely asymmetrical (i.e., keep talking, nobody explodes)
reasoning: The study is not a multiplayer or adversarial game; it is a set of standardized, identical tasks (mouse pointing test and typing test) given to all participants under the same conditions. There are no differentiated roles, abilities, or rule sets between participants, so by analogy to the rubric this is best treated as entirely symmetrical.
